patches_submitted.subject: [RFC PATCH] btrfs: trigger cow fixup via dirty_folio()

version_history.subject: [RFC PATCH] btrfs: trigger cow fixup via dirty_folio()

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch proposes a new approach to trigger the COW (Copy-On-Write) fixup in Btrfs via the dirty_folio() function, which is used to handle folios that have been improperly dirtied during writeback. The current implementation uses an asynchronous worker to catch and fix such cases, but this patch aims to simplify the process by leveraging the dirty_folio() function. This change addresses a long-standing issue where a dio read may skip dirtying a folio if it is already clean by the end of the I/O operation, leading to potential data corruption. The patch maintains three critical invariants to ensure that each block is written exactly once: any dirty block is covered by delalloc or an ordered extent, any dirty block submitted into an OE will be written back within that OE, and any dirty block already submitted into an OE will not be resubmitted. This change aims to demonstrate a more complex solution to the problem and highlight the issues it must address.

review_comments.author: Qu Wenruo
review_comments.summary: Qu Wenruo expressed concerns that the assumption in btrfs_folio_lock() about the relationship between dirty folios and ordered extents is incorrect, potentially causing false alerts when ->dirty_folio() callback is triggered for properly dirtied blocks. He suggested simplifying the check to just verify if the fixup bit is not set.

review_comments.author: Boris Burkov (author)
review_comments.summary: Author acknowledged that the delalloc lookup in btrfs_folio_cancel_fixup() can be simplified by checking if the fixup bit is not set, and agreed to rework it; also agreed to remove redundant comments and commit messages.

series_items.subject: [PATCH RFC v4 01/12] x86/mm: add untagged_addr_remote_unlocked()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new function, untagged_addr_remote_unlocked(), to the x86/mm module. The function is designed for callers that have not taken the mmap lock and allows them to access remote memory without asserting the lock. This is particularly useful in large machines running big multi-threaded applications where the mmap lock can be contended between readers and writers. The patch also annotates access to mm->context.untag_mask with READ_ONCE() and WRITE_ONCE() to make existing lockless reads explicit and KCSAN-clean.

series_items.subject: [PATCH RFC v4 02/12] riscv/mm: add untagged_addr_remote_unlocked()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series addresses a performance issue on large multi-threaded workloads where the mmap lock is contended, causing readers like /proc/PID/cmdline or process_vm_readv() to stall even when the target memory is resident. The solution involves adding an unlocked variant of untagged_addr_remote(), which masks the remote address against the target mm without asserting the lock.

series_items.subject: [PATCH RFC v4 03/12] mm: rename get_user_page_vma_remote() to get_user_page_lookup_vma()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch renames the function get_user_page_vma_remote() to get_user_page_lookup_vma() in the Linux kernel's memory management (mm) module. The renamed function still faults in a page at the specified address and looks up the VMA that covers it, but now with a more descriptive name that reflects its purpose of looking up the VMA. This change is intended to improve code readability and does not introduce any functional changes. The patch affects several files in the kernel, including arch-specific code and header files.

series_items.subject: [PATCH RFC v4 04/12] mm/gup: let check_vma_flags() ignore selected VMA flags
series_items.patch_summary: This patch allows the `check_vma_flags()` function to ignore specific VMA flags by adding an `ignore_flags` argument. This is useful for callers that need to handle exceptions in certain types of VMAs, such as COWed pages in VM_IO or VM_PFNMAP VMAs. The patch prepares for a future change where the `get_user_page_vma()` function will pass these specific flags to reach COWed pages. No functional changes are intended by this patch.

series_items.subject: [PATCH RFC v4 05/12] mm/gup: add get_user_page_vma() to fault in a page under a held lock
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new function, get_user_page_vma(), which allows faulting in a single page under a held lock. The function is designed to be used by __access_remote_vm() when it needs to access a page that is not already present in the page tables. It takes advantage of the existing VMA locking mechanism and simplifies the process of accessing remote memory. If the fault cannot complete under the per-VMA lock, the function releases the lock and returns -EAGAIN for both the mmap lock and the per-VMA lock. The patch also updates the handling of VM_FAULT_ERROR to return -EFAULT instead of BUG().

series_items.subject: [PATCH RFC v4 06/12] mm: use per-VMA lock in __access_remote_vm() for single-VMA accesses
series_items.patch_summary: This patch improves performance by reducing contention on the mmap_read_lock() in __access_remote_vm(). It introduces a per-VMA lock to access remote process memory when the access fits within one VMA, and falls back to the mmap_lock if necessary. The patch also optimizes page table walking under the per-VMA lock, making it safe against page table freeing and THP collapse. Additionally, it improves handling of COWed pages in VM_IO/VM_PFNMAP VMAs and adds a new access_remote_vma_ops() helper for accessing such memory.

series_items.subject: [PATCH RFC v4 07/12] mm: read remote strings under the per-VMA lock
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the __copy_remote_vm_str() function to read remote strings under a per-VMA lock instead of the mmap read lock, reducing contention and improving performance. The new implementation uses the existing remote_vm_walk() function with a copy_vm_str() action that copies each page and stops at the NUL character. If the string is too long, it falls back to the original mmap lock path. This change aims to improve the efficiency of reading strings from other processes' memory spaces.

series_items.subject: [PATCH RFC v4 08/12] selftests/mm: cover /proc/pid/mem access to VM_PFNMAP memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds two tests to the selftests/mm/pfnmap.c file to cover reading VM_PFNMAP memory through /proc/pid/mem. The first test, procmem_cow_read, maps a private and writable file, writes to a copy-on-write (COW) page, and then reads it back through /proc/self/mem. Without the struct-page path in get_user_page_vma(), this read would fall back to generic_access_phys() and ioremap of a COWed RAM page is rejected. The second test, procmem_pfn_read, reads a raw PFN back through ->access(). This patch exercises __access_remote_vm() two ways: through the struct-page path in get_user_page_vma() and through vma->vm_ops->access(), which ioremaps the PFN.

series_items.subject: [PATCH RFC v4 09/12] mm/gup: build get_user_page_lookup_vma() on get_user_page_vma()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch refactors the `get_user_page_lookup_vma()` function to reuse the existing `get_user_page_vma()` helper, eliminating duplicated code and improving performance. The new implementation holds the mmap lock throughout the call, ensuring that the VMA remains valid even in case of a fault. It also preserves the foreign-access permission check and accessed-bit behavior. The patch removes the old implementation and adds an assertion to ensure that the caller holds the mmap lock.

series_items.subject: [PATCH RFC v4 10/12] mm/gup: pass an end address to follow_page_mask() and return a page count
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the follow_page_mask() function in the mm/gup module to return the number of contiguous pages covered by a page, rather than a bitmask representing the enclosing huge page. The function now takes an additional 'end' argument that bounds how far the walk looks, allowing for more efficient handling of large folios and preventing unnecessary scanning. This change is intended to facilitate batching PTE-mapped large folios in a later patch without introducing functional changes.

series_items.subject: [PATCH RFC v4 11/12] mm/gup: batch contiguous PTE-mapped large folios in follow_page_mask()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the handling of PTE-mapped large folios in the Linux kernel's memory management system. It introduces a new function, `folio_pte_batch_flags()`, which counts consecutive present PTEs that map contiguous pages of the same folio with uniform write bits. This allows for batched retrieval of contiguous runs of pages, reducing the number of page table walks required. The patch also ensures that per-PTE guarantees are maintained for the head page in a run. The optimization is particularly beneficial for large anonymous regions and has been measured to improve performance by up to 7.6 times.

series_items.subject: [PATCH RFC v4 12/12] selftests/mm: add a slow-GUP content and COW test for mTHP
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new test, mthp_gup_cow_test, to the Linux kernel selftests suite. The test checks that the slow get_user_pages() path correctly handles large folios (mTHP) and copy-on-write (COW) operations. It does this by pinning a region of memory on the slow path, writing a distinct pattern to each page, and then verifying that the kernel copies back the correct contents from the pinned pages after a COW operation. The test also reports how many pages are in contiguous large-folio runs, allowing for better coverage testing of kernels without mTHP support.

get_user_page_lookup_vma() faults in one page of a remote mm and returns it
together with the VMA that covers it. It open-codes that with
get_user_pages_remote() followed by vma_lookup(), duplicating the
single-page walk that get_user_page_vma() now provides.

Every caller already holds the mmap lock, and the helper needs it anyway:
get_user_pages_remote(locked=NULL) and vma_lookup() both rely on it.

Look the VMA up under the held mmap lock and fault the page in through
get_user_page_vma() without FOLL_VMA_LOCK, so the lock is held for the
whole call and never dropped. Force FOLL_REMOTE and FOLL_TOUCH to
preserve the foreign-access permission check and accessed-bit behavior
that get_user_pages_remote() applied before.

Add mmap_assert_locked() so the lock requirement is documented and any
future caller that forgets it trips the assertion rather than walking page
tables unlocked.

Reject FOLL_UNLOCKABLE alongside the existing FOLL_NOWAIT check: both let
the fault handler drop the mmap lock, which would invalidate the VMA looked
up here. get_user_page_vma() passes neither, so the lock is held for the
whole walk and the returned VMA stays valid.

The one behavioral change is that the old path could drop and retake the
mmap lock across a fault, while get_user_page_vma() holds it throughout.
None of the callers rely on the lock being dropped.

__access_remote_vm() reads another process's memory under the mmap lock. On
large machines running big multi-threaded applications, that lock is
contended between readers and writers: an mmap() or munmap() in one thread
stalls readers like /proc/PID/cmdline, /proc/PID/environ, or
process_vm_readv(), even though the memory they read is almost always
resident and reachable under the per-VMA lock instead.

Looking up the VMA first requires untagging the address.
untagged_addr_remote() asserts the mmap lock only because it reads
mm->context.untag_mask, which can race with the write in mm_enable_lam().

That mask changes only while the target is single-threaded, when it
enables LAM or resets it at exec. The read need not be stable: it is
already read locklessly elsewhere, and a remote untag is best-effort.

Add untagged_addr_remote_unlocked() for callers that have not taken the
mmap lock, and annotate access to mm->context.untag_mask with READ_ONCE()
and WRITE_ONCE() so the existing lockless reads are explicit and
KCSAN-clean. untagged_addr_remote() keeps its assertion and shares the same
code.

review_comments.raw_body:
__access_remote_vm() holds mmap_read_lock() for the whole transfer. On
large machines, with large multi-threaded applications, the mmap_lock
is often contended, leading to things like reads of /proc/PID/cmdline
stalling.

This results in system monitoring tools getting stuck, right when
system information would be the most helpful.

That problem can be avoided by having __access_remote_vm() access
user memory under the per-VMA lock. The old code also looks up
the VMA for every page accessed, and walks the page tables for
every page inside a large folio. Cleaning that up speeds things
up nicely.

Using code that does not include its own lock dance, and does not
look up the VMA twice results in a modest speedup.

	read size   baseline    per-VMA     throughput
	8 B          201.7 ns    170.6 ns    ~15% faster
	4 KB         495 ns      442 ns      +12% (8266 -> 9265 MB/s)
	64 KB       4115 ns     3355 ns      +23% (15927 -> 19536 MB/s)
	1 MB       75902 ns    63641 ns      +19% (13815 -> 16477 MB/s)

The multi-threaded reader-versus-writer contention that motivates the lock
is not measured.

The rest of the series builds on this to batch per-VMA GUP. Patches 9-12
have follow_page_mask() report a contiguous PTE-mapped run of a large
folio, so the slow pin_user_pages() path walks it once instead of per page.
Other paths that walk a range benefit too.

That batching pays off on PTE-mapped mTHP. With mm/gup_test.c
(PIN_LONGTERM_BENCHMARK, the slow pin_user_pages() path) on a 256 MB
MADV_HUGEPAGE region in a 4 CPU VM, median get time over 16 iterations:

	gup_test -L -m 256 -n 65536 -r 16 -t
	                      before      after
	64 kB mTHP            3140 us      412 us   (7.6x)
	2 MB THP (control)      78 us       76 us
	4 kB base (control)   3010 us     3042 us

The PMD-mapped 2 MB THP already returns in one step, so only the PTE-mapped
large folio case improves.

Reaching a page under the per-VMA lock means looking up the VMA first,
which needs to untag the remote address without the mmap lock. The untag
masks (x86 LAM, riscv pointer masking) change only while the target is
single-threaded, so a remote reader races at most one such change.

Those masks are already read locklessly elsewhere, so patches 1 and 2 add
untagged_addr_remote_unlocked() helpers with READ_ONCE()/WRITE_ONCE()
annotations. A stale read sees the old or new mask, never a torn value, and
the remote untag is best-effort.

With the VMA in hand we need one page from it under the lock the caller
already holds. get_user_pages_remote() does not fit: it hard codes the mmap
lock and re-derives the VMA internally.

Rather than reimplement GUP in yet another caller, this version follows
David Hildenbrand's v2 guidance: start from a proper GUP interface that
takes a locked VMA, not an mm, and decide which faults can resolve under
the VMA lock.

Patch 3 renames get_user_page_vma_remote() to get_user_page_lookup_vma() to
free the name. Patch 5 adds get_user_page_vma(): a simplified
__get_user_pages() that walks the tables with follow_page_mask(), faults a
missing page in with faultin_page(), and returns it with a reference and
the caller's lock still held.

Like __get_user_pages() it runs check_vma_flags(), so callers need not
pre-check the VMA.

A VM_IO or VM_PFNMAP VMA is the exception: a COWed page with a struct page
is returned normally, while a raw PFN yields -EFAULT so the caller can
reach vma->vm_ops->access(). The caller sets FOLL_VMA_LOCK when it holds
the per-VMA lock, which reaches the fault code as FAULT_FLAG_VMA_LOCK.

Anything the per-VMA lock cannot finish releases the lock and returns
-EAGAIN, so the caller retries under the mmap lock: a dropped fault, a
userfaultfd VMA (which assumes current is the faulting task), a hard error,
or ->access() memory. faultin_page() reports the retry the same way for
both lock types.

__access_remote_vm() then uses the per-VMA lock when an access fits within
one VMA, and falls back to the mmap lock for multi-VMA accesses, stack
expansion, or an -EAGAIN from get_user_page_vma().

Walking page tables under only the per-VMA lock is safe against both page
table freeing and THP collapse. munmap() frees a VMA's page tables under
the VMA write lock that our read lock excludes, so they cannot be torn down
under the walk.

THP collapse needs neither lock: it retracts a PTE page under the page
table lock and frees it by RCU.

follow_page_pte() takes that same lock through pte_offset_map_lock() and
rechecks the pmd, so it either walks an intact table or sees the collapsed
pmd and faults the page in, while RCU keeps the retracted page valid.

A COWed page in a VM_PFNMAP mapping was previously unreachable through
/proc/pid/mem because generic_access_phys() rejects ioremaps of RAM. With
get_user_page_vma() returning the struct page directly, that read now
succeeds, which the new selftests cover along with the raw PFN path.

Thanks to Suren for pointing out the need, to David for pushing me
to just rework the whole area, to Usama for reviewing the arch patches,
and Lorenzo for the changelog and cover letter cleanups.

There is a lot more work that could be done in this area, but the
patch series is big enough. More changes can come in follow up work.

review_comments.author: Rik Riel (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed concerns about the locking behavior in __access_remote_vm() and get_user_pages_remote(), acknowledging that they hard-coded the mmap lock and re-looked up the VMA, neither of which is desired here. The author proposed a new function, get_user_page_vma(), to simplify the process, which faults in a missing page under either the mmap lock or the per-VMA lock, with the caller's lock still held.

review_comments.author: Mike Rapoport
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer Mike Rapoport noted that the patch does not address the locking issue in __access_remote_vm, which acquires the per-vswap spinlock while holding the folio lock, creating a potential deadlock with reclaim paths.

Reviewer Mike Rapoport requested the use of ksft_* helpers for printing messages and tracking failed and passed tests, but did not specifically address the patch's per-VMA lock implementation.
